title: crypto2dev_cipher: IV guard 'iv \!= NULL && ivSz > 0 && ivSz <= CRYPTO2DEV_IV_MAXLEN' silently skips oversized IV
description: In crypto2dev_cipher() at port.c:685, the SET_IV call is guarded by 'iv \!= NULL && ivSz > 0 && ivSz <= CRYPTO2DEV_IV_MAXLEN'. If ivSz > CRYPTO2DEV_IV_MAXLEN (32 bytes), SET_IV is silently skipped and INIT proceeds without an IV. For CBC (AES_BLOCK_SIZE=16) and CTR (16) this is impossible in practice since their IVs are always AES_BLOCK_SIZE=16. For GCM with non-standard IV sizes (> 32 bytes) this would silently proceed with no IV, and the device's behavior is undefined. Better: check 'ivSz > CRYPTO2DEV_IV_MAXLEN' explicitly and return BUFFER_E, mirroring the AAD check. Suggested rewrite: separate the null/zero guard from the size guard, returning BAD_FUNC_ARG on null/zero and BUFFER_E on oversized.
